p2.head:
# Review Packet — Part 2: Manual Mobility & General DME

**For:** Manual Mobility (Parth Dave, Manager)
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-2-Manual-Mobility-and-General-DME-v3.0* (Word), or Part 2 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **2.4.1**.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from current Medicare guidance, not from your team's guide. Please confirm each one reflects how your team works.

rows.says: **Out-of-pocket purchases are handled by the CSR team**, who then email intake, eligibility and Field Operations. They're no longer transferred to the Manual Mobility queue
rows.why: Your team now receives these by email rather than as a transfer

rows.says: **Wheelchair coverage by code**, per Medicare: K0001–K0003 are defined as 250 lbs or less; K0004 has no capacity limit; **K0006** is covered for a patient **over 250 lbs**; **K0007** for a patient **over 300 lbs**
rows.why: Replaces the earlier wording, which gave 250 and 450 lb thresholds for the extra-wide and bariatric chairs

rows.says: **Both extra-wide chairs — the Guardian Extra Wide and the Shuttle — are K0007**, so Medicare covers them only over 300 lbs
rows.why: The previous guide said the extra-wide chair needed documentation "over 250 lbs" and the bariatric chair "over 450 lbs." **Is 450 lbs something your team uses to choose between the two chairs?**

rows.says: **Medline K3 Guardian 20"** — 300 lb capacity, billed as **K0006**, or K0003 with the E2201 wide-seat add-on
rows.why: Newly added. Note for Billing: at 300 lbs this chair fits the K0006 definition; K0003 is defined as 250 lbs or less

rows.says: **Bariatric walker threshold: over 300 lbs**
rows.why: The previous guide said "above 301 lbs." Medicare's threshold is over 300

rows.says: **Every hospital bed needs clinical notes from the last 6 months.** The **bariatric bed (E0301)** also needs a face-to-face encounter and a written order **before delivery**
rows.why: The E0301 requirement comes from CMS's list of items requiring a pre-delivery face-to-face, which added some heavy-duty beds in 2024

rows.says: **New nebulizer orders stay with Manual Mobility; refill supplies are handled by Resupply** (now in Part 3, 3.3.3, with Medicare's allowances)
rows.why: The supplies table used to live in Part 2

rows.says: **Uncommon payers** — Workers' Compensation or the VA, for example — may pay for an item in full, **including the upgrade fee**
rows.why: New note

rows.says: The waiver rules are now also shown as a **decision diagram**: QMB-only is checked first, because it waives the standard rollator fee only
rows.why: Please look over the diagram as well as the table

groups.title: Stated in the manual, not taken from your guide — please verify

rows.says: **Weight capacities:** Medline K4 High-Strength and Hybrid 2 — **300 lbs**; Medline K3 Guardian (16"–18") and Guardian Reclining — **250 lbs**
**Lift chairs are Texas-only**, through the Medicaid Waiver Program — not a general Texas Medicaid benefit
**Bathroom items:** the 3-in-1 commode can be covered by Medicare anywhere; shower chairs and tub benches are Texas Medicaid only; the raised toilet seat is out-of-pocket only

groups.title: Carried over from your guide — still accurate?

rows.says: **Walkers are never shipped out of state** — an out-of-state walker order is out of range (OOR)
Other items have a **delivery radius measured in distance**, varying by item. **The manual doesn't give the radii or say where CSRs find them.** What are they, or where should CSRs look?
**Shared codes:** E0143 is both the front-wheeled walker and the basic steel rollator; E0149 is both the bariatric walker and the heavy-duty rollator
**The bariatric bed has no upgrade fee**, needs its own medical necessity documentation, and its rails can't be changed after delivery
A patient can **change wheelchair size before validation**; after validation the order has to be reopened
**Rollator weights:** basic steel 19 lbs, heavy-duty 24 lbs
**Knee walkers** are out-of-pocket, except through VGM Homelink
**Blood pressure monitors:** wrist monitor only — no arm cuff

**Upgrade fees** (intake / Field Ops): standard rollator $55 / $85 · heavy-duty rollator $97 / $127 · fully-electric bed $550 / $850 · Hi-Lo bed $580 / $880 · battery lift $1,207 / $1,357 · heavy-duty battery lift $2,495 / $2,645

groups.title: Open questions

rows.q: **What do you wish a CSR had already collected before transferring a call to your team?**
Is anything your team handles **missing** from Part 2 — something CSRs get asked about but won't find?
Does Part 2 describe anything your team **no longer does**, or does differently now?

p3.head:
# Review Packet — Part 3: Respiratory & Resupply

**For:** Respiratory & Resupply (Nikunj Solanki, Manager)
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-3-Respiratory-and-Resupply-v3.0* (Word), or Part 3 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **3.7.4**.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from current Medicare guidance, not from your team's guide. Please confirm each one reflects how your team works.

rows.says: **Resupply processes the initial order** for oxygen concentrators and ventilators — requesting and reviewing the provider's documents, and submitting to insurance. After delivery, **oxygen service and supplies** are CSR service tickets, and **a ventilator problem** goes to the Service Q
rows.why: Makes explicit who owns a respiratory machine before and after delivery

rows.says: **Picking up a respiratory machine** follows the normal process: the CSR creates the pick-up ticket unless the item is patient-owned, and **the responsible team requests any further documents** from the MDO
rows.why: The previous guide said a machine couldn't be picked up without a discontinue prescription. That's no longer a CSR prerequisite

rows.says: **A prescription is required even for an out-of-pocket purchase** of an oxygen concentrator, **a PAP device (CPAP or BiPAP)**, or a ventilator — federal law restricts their sale to a prescriber's order
rows.why: **PAP devices are new to this rule.** The previous guide named concentrators and ventilators only

rows.says: **Out-of-pocket purchases are handled by the CSR team**, who email intake, eligibility and Field Operations. They're no longer routed to the Resupply queue
rows.why: Your team now receives these by email

rows.says: **Compliance — notes first.** CSRs answer from the compliance specialists' notes — compliant-through date, documents being requested, or confirmed non-compliant with a pick-up started — and transfer only when the notes don't settle it
rows.why: Replaces "always transfer compliance calls." Compliance, including the item list, now lives in 3.12 rather than an appendix

rows.says: **Resupply emails** use the category as the subject line's update type: `Trach Resupply: John Doe 123456`, `Incontinence Resupply: …`, `CPAP Resupply: …`
rows.why: The manual's email format changed to `[Update type]: [Patient name] [TRX #]`

rows.says: **Nebulizer refill supplies are now handled here**, with Medicare's allowances and a **three-month maximum per shipment**. New nebulizer orders stay with Manual Mobility
rows.why: Moved from Part 2

rows.says: **Texas Medicaid**: billed one month at a time, eligibility checked before each shipment, and the Title XIX order covers deliveries for up to **six months** from the provider's signature
rows.why: New note, from the Texas Medicaid provider manual

rows.says: **Resupply timing (Medicare):** the patient confirms the refill **within the 30 days** before their supply runs out, and we ship **no sooner than 10 days** before. For a shipped order, **the ship date is the date of service**
rows.why: **The contact window changed from 14 days to 30.** CMS moved to 30 days, and codified it in January 2024

rows.says: **After hours, a ventilator issue** means dispatching the on-call RT **immediately**, without troubleshooting
rows.why: New line, matching Part 8

rows.says: **Documents can be sent and received by fax, email, Parachute or SutureSign** — on any order type
rows.why: Previously described as a respiratory-only exception

groups.title: Stated in the manual, not taken from your guide — please verify

rows.says: **Nebulizer supply allowances** (Medicare): administration set 2/month · nebulizer kit 2/month, in addition to the set · disposable filter 2/month · aerosol mask 1/month · water collection device 2/month

**PAP compliance** (Medicare): at least 4 hours a night on 70% of nights in a consecutive 30-day period within the first 90 days, **and** a face-to-face re-evaluation between day 31 and day 91. A failed trial needs a new evaluation **and** a repeat facility-based sleep test

**CPAP (E0601) and BiPAP (E0470) are capped rentals**; **E0471 is a continuous monthly rental**, never owned. Switching from a CPAP that proved ineffective during titration or the home trial needs no new evaluation or sleep test; after more than 3 months of use it needs a new evaluation, but not a new sleep test
**What each compliance item requires** — including a ventilator hold being escalated the same day

groups.title: Carried over from your guide — still accurate?

rows.says: **No portable oxygen concentrators** — home units only. Concentrator servicing stays with CSR, not the Service Q
The **trach tube** is the only trach item not replaced monthly — **1 per 3 months**
**PAP supply allowances**, including heated tubing at 1 per 3 months
**Incontinence allowances** (Texas Medicaid): wipes 2 packs/month · underpads 120/month · briefs 240/month · pull-ups 240/month · liners 240/month
**No new orders for external or Purewick catheters** — intermittent only. Patients already receiving external catheters may continue
If an MDO asks about a **ventilator referral we can't find**, check with the Respiratory & Resupply Manager before saying it wasn't received
**No new IPPB units.** If Service and the RTs are both unavailable, email both `respiratory@` and `service@`
**Resupply category owners:** CPAP — Sonia S. · Incontinence and catheter — Michelle B. · Trach, suction and ventilator — Monica J. None currently has a backup
**Oximetry testing** — we can facilitate it

groups.title: Open questions

rows.q: **What do you wish a CSR had already collected before transferring a call to your team?**
Is anything your team handles **missing** from Part 3 — something CSRs get asked about but won't find?
Does Part 3 describe anything your team **no longer does**, or does differently now?

**3.7.1 — APAP** (added 2026-10-07). An APAP bills as E0601, the CPAP code, so E0601 documentation covers either, and the **Luna G3 X APAP (G4600)**, now in the CPAP table, works as either. Is that right? When a patient switches from a fixed pressure to auto, does the provider need to send a new pressure order?

p4.head:
# Review Packet — Part 4: Power Mobility

**For:** Power intake — **Erica Thongvan** (PAK) and **Ahmed Ramadan** (Qualifications)
**Also for:** **Ozaire (MD) Hawa** (Field Ops-Power) — questions marked **◆**
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-4-Power-Mobility-v3.0* (Word), or Part 4 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **4.7.2**. Power was Part 3 in earlier drafts.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from current Medicare guidance, not from your team's guide. Please confirm each one reflects how your teams work.

rows.says: **The Power Order Process diagram** — four phases: Intake and education (PAK), Qualifications, Verification & authorization, and Delivery. Sales feeds in two ways: at *Eligible* (appointment confirmed and insurance verified), or directly to Qualifications when a **mobility evaluation was done in the last 6 months**
rows.why: Replaces the process image from your guide. Please check the phases, the order, and the two ways in

rows.says: **Documents Qualifications reviews and requests.** Always: **M.E. F2F, SWO, SE, LCMP Declaration, MRx**. When applicable: **Addendum, PT/OT Report Concurrence**. With a PT evaluation: **PT Rx, PT Report**. With an ATP evaluation: **ATP Report**
rows.why: Is the list complete, and is each in the right group?

rows.says: **Typical times:** PAR decision in **14 days or less**; appeals **up to a month**; **2–3 weeks** from the manufacturer order to our warehouse. **If the appeals are also denied, the order is closed**
rows.why: The closed-order outcome is new

rows.says: **A Qualified Lead skips PAK, but still gets a PPD** — conducted by a Qualifications team member rather than the PPD team
rows.why: New clarification

rows.says: **Order verification** happens after any PT or ATP evaluation, can overlap Qualifications or PAR, and **must be complete before the manufacturer order**. The manual says **Field Ops-Power** calls the patient to do it. ◆
rows.why: Please confirm both the timing and who does it

rows.says: **Field Ops-Power Q (ext 344) takes scheduling** — delivery, ATP evaluations, and service visits once a repair is arranged. **A patient reporting a problem with their PMD goes to the Service Q**, which starts the service request ◆
rows.why: Replaces "all Power-related calls go to Field Ops-Power"

rows.says: **ATP evaluations** are scheduled by Field Ops-Power, **up to 2–3 weeks out depending on the ATP's travel route**. **Virtual ATP evaluations** — the uncommon remote case — are scheduled only by Erica Thongvan ◆

**Returns:** PWCs generally aren't picked up, but once the repair and affordability checks are clear, **the CSR still creates the pick-up ticket** — whether the chair is collected or written off is decided afterward, and neither is promised ◆
rows.why: Previously read as "we don't pick them up," which could lead a CSR to refuse the request

rows.says: **An insurance rep giving a PAR decision:** the CSR records the decision and reference number, confirms the letter will be faxed or emailed, posts notes, and **emails the Power intake team** — no transfer
rows.why: The previous guide said "no further action needed," with no email to intake

rows.says: **Email subject lines:** `PT Eval: [Patient name] [TRX #]` and `Authorization Request: [Patient name] [TRX #]`
rows.why: The manual's email format changed to `[Update type]: [Patient name] [TRX #]`

rows.says: **Delivery** is to the patient's home — never a facility — and the patient must be home. **Freight calls:** get the freight company's name and the city they're delivering to, then transfer to Field Ops-Power, relaying both ◆
**Repairs:** who pays depends on **rental status and warranty**, not time since delivery. Patients are told to report issues as soon as possible
rows.why: The previous guide suggested coverage lapsed "months later"

rows.says: **The 90-day figure:** CSRs may say the national average for this type of order is about 90 days and that UMS is faster — but that actual time varies with the paperwork, and then give the current stage
**Sales Eligibility** can be reached by email (`saleseligibility@`) or direct transfer to its supervisor, April Arredondo — go to her where possible

groups.title: Stated in the manual, not taken from your guide — please verify

rows.says: **Power wheelchairs need a face-to-face encounter and a written order before delivery** — a Medicare requirement by statute
**PWCs are capped rentals** at 15% of the purchase price for months 1–3 and 6% for months 4–13; the patient owns the chair after 13 paid months
**A patient who surrenders a PMD** may not be able to get another for five years under the Same or Similar rule

groups.title: Carried over from your guide — still accurate?

rows.says: **The PPD** is a ~15-minute interview on the patient's mobility issues, PMD options and the process. Afterwards the PAK team sends links to a **consent form and an AOR form** — neither mandatory, both used for appeals
**The Seating Evaluation mistake:** the PAK includes a pre-filled SE watermarked "Patient Provided Data" as a guide, plus two blank SE pages for the provider to complete
**A documentation request older than 3 days** — confirm the fax number, ask for a backup, re-fax; offer secure email if the MDO is hard to reach
An ATP visit noted as a **"drive-by"** still gets transferred to Field Ops-Power if the patient calls ◆
**An MA plan is the primary**, not a secondary. Where an order goes to both Medicare and an MA plan, the Authorization team submits to both at once or in sequence
**PAR specialists:** Kadija S. (standard PWC) and Ashton E. (complex PWC and appeals). Neither currently has a backup
**POVs aren't eligible for ROHO cushions.** Out-of-pocket POV pricing runs roughly **$1,200–$1,900**
**No vehicle lifts** of any kind; **ramps** are out-of-pocket only; **cup holders** can be added (after delivery, through Service)

groups.title: Open questions

rows.q: **What do you wish a CSR had already collected before transferring a call to your team?** Please answer separately for PAK, Qualifications and Field Ops-Power if the answers differ
Is anything your teams handle **missing** from Part 4 — something CSRs get asked about but won't find?
Does Part 4 describe anything your teams **no longer do**, or do differently now?

**9.4.1 (in Part 9) — a past PMD patient who wants a new PMD** (added 2026-10-07). Five years or more since the last PMD was delivered → Sales creates a new order on the existing account. Within five years → usually a Same or Similar conflict, with a possible exception when the new PMD is an **upgrade** and the provider attests to a **significant change in physical condition or mobility needs**; for now this call also goes to **Sales**, and 4.1 points there. Is all of this right? Should the within-five-years call go to Power instead, and who decides whether the provider's attestation is enough?

p5.head:
# Review Packet — Part 5: Field Operations

**For:** Field Operations — **Parth Shah** (Manager) and **Mahesh Patel** (Supervisor)
**Also for:** **Ozaire (MD) Hawa** (Field Ops-Power) — questions marked **◆**
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-5-Field-Operations-v3.0* (Word), or Part 5 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **5.9.2**.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from current Medicare guidance, not from your team's guide. Please confirm each one reflects how your team works.

rows.says: The Field Ops-Power Q (ext 344) takes Power scheduling — delivery, ATP evaluations, and service visits once a repair is arranged. A patient reporting a problem with their PMD goes to the Service Q ◆
rows.why: Replaces "all Power-related calls go to Field Ops-Power, including PMD service or repair"

rows.says: Every pick-up: the CSR tells the caller Field Ops will verify the request and **call back within 24–48 hours** to confirm if and when it can happen
rows.why: A new commitment made on your team's behalf. Is 24–48 hours right for all pick-ups?

rows.says: A pick-up ticket includes the reason, the **best contact, the pick-up address, and access instructions**
rows.why: The pick-up address was added, and the empty "date constraints" row was removed

rows.says: PMD pick-up requests: uncomfortable or adjustable → Service · technical fault → Service · can't afford it → the EAA or a payment plan first · patient-owned → can't be picked up · otherwise, create the ticket ◆
rows.why: Two versions of this table, in Parts 5 and 6, have been merged into one here, with a decision diagram

rows.says: The EAA is processed by Billing. A CSR or Billing sends the blank form from the CSR shared drive; the patient returns it with their income and expenses; usually 1–2 weeks. Out-of-pocket orders qualify for neither the EAA nor a payment plan
rows.why: The EAA process wasn't described before

rows.says: Hospital bed relocation: either a Field Ops supervisor or a Service supervisor decides, and a CSR routes the call to Service. Generally not done — possible within the Dallas, San Antonio and Hawaii areas, rental beds only, $150
rows.why: Previously said it had to be verified by the Field Operations Supervisor alone

rows.says: Resupply timing (Medicare): the patient confirms the refill within the 30 days before their supply runs out; we ship no sooner than 10 days before. For a shipped order, the ship date is the date of service
rows.why: The contact window changed from 14 days to 30, per CMS

rows.says: Freight company calls: get the company's name and the city they're delivering to, then transfer to Field Ops-Power, relaying both ◆
Used equipment: items that need a prescription for out-of-pocket purchase still need one — oxygen concentrators, PAP devices (CPAP and BiPAP), and ventilators
rows.why: PAP devices were added: federal law restricts their sale to a prescriber's order

rows.says: After a patient dies: if the equipment isn't patient-owned, the CSR confirms the best contact and pick-up address and creates a ticket; Field Ops verifies and calls back within 24–48 hours. A family who'd rather pay the remaining cost and keep the items goes to Billing
rows.why: These tickets come to your team

groups.title: Stated in the manual, not taken from your guide — please verify

rows.says: The two-day rule: equipment may be delivered to a hospital or nursing facility no earlier than two days before discharge, for fitting or training only. If discharge moves, the item is picked up and redelivered
During a Medicare Part A SNF stay, consolidated billing makes the facility responsible for the patient's equipment. An assisted living facility generally counts as the patient's home
Supplies can't be shipped until the patient is discharged — the two-day window covers equipment, not supplies
What every proof of delivery must contain, and that it's kept for seven years from the date of service
Backorders: Field Ops proactively updates the patient; no estimated date is given unless the manufacturer has provided one

groups.title: Carried over from your guide — still accurate?

rows.says: Field Ops or Service: validated but not delivered → Field Ops · delivered, and the caller says it was wrong → Service · delivered same day with items missing and no Delivered icon yet → Field Ops · mask fitting → Field Ops Q
Routing rules for common calls — callbacks to a scheduling message, discharge dates, deliveries "verified via documentation," and PMD dates differing by 1–3 days
The driver or technician calls 30–60 minutes before arrival; builds equipment on site; adjusts and instructs on PMDs
For a hospital bed, the patient must clear the space in advance
A PMD is never delivered to a facility, and the patient must be present ◆
The Purchase Capped Rental Form is signed at delivery; check Artifacts for it before conceding a "nobody told me" call
Emergency overnight shipping is possible for respiratory supplies if the patient pays the difference — contact the Field Operations Supervisor
The used equipment pool is limited — most commonly PWC K0821 and K0823, and CPAP
An order with a paid upgrade fee can be returned unused within 15 days, less a non-refundable 20% restocking fee; after 15 days the fee isn't refundable
Oximetry devices: delivery and pick-up are scheduled together, so a pick-up can appear before the item shows as delivered

groups.title: Open questions

rows.q: **What do you wish a CSR had already collected before transferring a call to your team?** Please answer separately for Field Ops and Field Ops-Power if they differ
Is anything your team handles **missing** from Part 5 — something CSRs get asked about but won't find?
Does Part 5 describe anything your team **no longer does**, or does differently now?

p6.head:
# Review Packet — Part 6: Service

**For:** Service — **Arnav Pan** (Supervisor)
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-6-Service-v3.0* (Word), or Part 6 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **6.3.2**.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from current Medicare guidance, not from your team's guide. Please confirm each one reflects how your team works.

rows.says: Who pays for a repair depends on **rental status and warranty**, not time since delivery. A patient can't be charged a service charge, curb-side fee or delivery charge while their equipment is being repaired
rows.why: Replaces wording that implied coverage lapsed with time. The no-trip-charge rule comes from Medicare's supplier requirements

rows.says: A **$75 out-of-pocket charge** applies to a diagnostic-only visit where no service or repair turns out to be needed. CSRs say so **before** booking; there's no charge if a repair is performed
rows.why: New section

rows.says: **Loaners:** CSRs don't raise them unprompted. A loaner is possible only while patient-owned equipment is being repaired, and Service confirms — not during the rental period, and not while waiting for a new device
rows.why: Previously described loaners more generally

rows.says: A patient **reporting a problem with their PMD** comes to the Service Q. Once Service has arranged the repair, the visit is scheduled through the Field Ops-Power Q
rows.why: The split between reporting a problem and scheduling the visit is new

rows.says: **PMD pick-up requests:** discomfort, fit problems and technical faults come to Service rather than becoming a pick-up. The full table now lives in 5.9.2, with a decision diagram
rows.why: The two versions of this table, in Parts 5 and 6, were merged

rows.says: **Warranties:** Service requests coverage, and the manufacturer decides whether it applies
rows.why: Previously read as though UMS approved warranties

rows.says: **Irreparable damage** means a specific accident or natural disaster, such as a fire or flood — Medicare's definition. Damage from neglect, like a chair left out in the rain, doesn't qualify. The incident has to be documented
rows.why: Previously suggested rain damage might qualify for a covered replacement

rows.says: **After hours, a ventilator issue** means dispatching the on-call RT immediately, without troubleshooting
rows.why: New line, matching Part 8

rows.says: **Hospital bed relocation:** either a Field Ops or a Service supervisor decides, and **a CSR routes the call to Service**. If approved: Service ticket, validated by Service, pushed to Field Ops for scheduling

**Swap-outs:** if the change needs new documents from the MDO — a different or additional HCPCS code, or a new MRx — the CSR creates a pick-up ticket, notes it to coordinate with the new delivery, and emails intake. If not, it goes to Service for a swap-out ticket
The only ventilator UMS carries is the **Trilogy**; ventilator and cough assist issues go to the Service Q

groups.title: Stated in the manual, not taken from your guide — please verify

rows.says: **Where the repair table doesn't apply:** oxygen equipment, ventilators and E0471 devices, capped rentals still in their rental period, and anything under warranty
**Patient-owned equipment** (month 14 or later): Medicare covers medically necessary repairs and parts, and the deductible and coinsurance apply
**Lost or stolen equipment:** a police report is required before a replacement request can be submitted — it's the entry requirement, not a guarantee

groups.title: Carried over from your guide — still accurate?

rows.says: **The routing table** — including the resupply distinction: items that differ from the transaction go to Service; items that match but aren't what the patient expected go to Resupply
**Warranty periods:** usually 1 year, sometimes 6 months or 2 years. Water damage is the common way one is voided
**Complex respiratory service** routes through the Service Q; oxygen concentrator servicing stays with CSR
**CPAP set-up and instruction:** Service creates the ticket, and Field Ops schedules an RT
**Chargers and batteries** can be sold out of pocket even to callers who didn't get their PMD from us, depending on warehouse availability
**Turnaround** varies widely and isn't quoted as a range
Notes marked **"(For internal use only)"** aren't relayed to patients, and a tracking date in a note isn't given as a delivery date
A patient calling back about one of our **outbound service calls** is routed to the Service Q

**A PMD we can no longer service** — suggest a local DME repair service; for insurance to pay, it must be enrolled with or in network for the patient's plan. The competitor referrals (Numotion, WSR, National Seating & Mobility) were removed
rows.why: Changed 2026-10-07 at the Customer Service Manager's direction. Should any referral guidance replace it?

groups.title: Open questions

rows.q: **Does your team have troubleshooting guides** for power wheelchairs, or for any other equipment category? If so, please provide them — they'd let CSRs, including after hours, work through basic checks before a service request is created
**What do you wish a CSR had already collected before transferring a call to your team?**
Is anything your team handles **missing** from Part 6 — something CSRs get asked about but won't find?
Does Part 6 describe anything your team **no longer does**, or does differently now?

p7.head:
# Review Packet — Part 7: Oxygen

**For:** **Nikunj Solanki** (Respiratory & Resupply) — oxygen supplies, initial orders, compliance and the rental rules
**Also for:** **Arnav Pan** (Service) — concentrator servicing and troubleshooting, questions marked **◆**
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-7-Oxygen-v3.0* (Word), or Part 7 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **7.2.1**.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from current Medicare guidance, not from your team's guide. Please confirm each one reflects how your teams work.

rows.says: **A new oxygen patient:** Resupply processes the initial order — documents and insurance — and CSR work starts once the concentrator is delivered
rows.why: Makes the handoff between Resupply and CSR explicit

rows.says: **Oxygen tanks are a rental accessory, not a resupply item**, so the resupply contact and shipping windows don't apply. The limit is once a week, with 2 business days' notice

**Oxygen accessories are included for the full 5 years** — through the 36-month rental and, after it, in months 37–60, when the supplier must keep providing them with no separate payment. A patient shouldn't see a bill for cannulas or tubing at any point
rows.why: Previously said "during the 36-month rental period" only. CMS Policy Article A52514 extends it through the useful lifetime

rows.says: **The conserver is included in the oxygen rental, not billed.** If the provider orders one, we supply it at no charge; without an order it's $320 out of pocket, with an ABN for Medicare patients. It's coded **A9900**
rows.why: Previously described as needing a prescription "for insurance coverage," and coded E1352. Medicare's oxygen accessory list names conserving devices as A9900, included in the rental

rows.says: **Compliance — notes first.** CSRs answer from the compliance specialists' notes and transfer only when the notes don't settle it
rows.why: Replaces "compliance calls go to the Compliance Specialist"

rows.says: **The patient doesn't own the concentrator.** After 36 months rental billing stops, but UMS keeps ownership and keeps furnishing the equipment, supplies and servicing for up to 5 years
**The troubleshooting flowchart** — the emergency check comes first, then troubleshooting only for a patient who's stable and on a backup **cylinder**, then a technician visit if it's still faulty ◆
rows.why: Redrawn from your guide's flowchart. "Switch to their portable system" became "switch to a cylinder," since we don't carry portable concentrators

rows.says: **After hours,** the same flowchart applies, but where it says to schedule a technician visit, the CSR dispatches the on-call DME technician instead ◆
**Reorder at least 2 business days ahead**, matching the ordering rule
rows.why: Previously said 48 hours, which differs over a weekend

groups.title: Stated in the manual, not taken from your guide — please verify

rows.says: **A short break in need** — 60 days plus the rest of that rental month — resumes the existing rental
**What restarts the 36 months** — including a switch from Medicare Advantage to fee-for-service, which resumes with no new blood gas test
**Replacement after the 5-year useful lifetime is all or nothing** — stationary and portable equipment are replaced together, starting a new 36 months

groups.title: Carried over from your guide — still accurate?

rows.says: **We only supply oxygen to patients who received their concentrator from us.** A patient with another supplier's concentrator returns it there, then has their provider send us a referral

**Ordering rules:** 2 business days' lead time (same or next day for Irving office pick-up) · once a week · up to 10 tanks per delivery, generally 6 · the same number of empties collected · at least one E cylinder at home · M6 and E cylinders only
**Creating an oxygen supply ticket** — the steps and screenshots
**Same-day tanks** can be created on request, with the patient told the standard is 2 business days
**Power outage** — check they have their E cylinder, then create a same-day ticket
**Supply allowances** — cannulas come in packs of 4 with 7 ft tubing; add humidifier adapter tubing whenever a bottle is ordered
**Concentrators:** home units only, 5 LPM and 10 LPM ◆
**Cylinder durations** — at 2 LPM, an M6 lasts about 1.4 hours and an E about 5.7
**Maintenance:** the patient cleans the filter weekly; we schedule a maintenance visit every 6 months ◆
**Facility stays** where the patient still needs oxygen aren't a break in need

# Review Packet — Part 8: After Hours

**For:** After-hours coverage — **Robin** (Customer Service Manager), **Parth Shah** and **Shagun Shastri**
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-8-After-Hours-v3.0* (Word), or Part 8 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **8.4**.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from current Medicare guidance, not from the after-hours guide. Please confirm each one reflects how after hours actually runs.

rows.says: **Escalation step 5:** if no one responds, **repeat from step 1** — and if distress develops at any point, 9-1-1 comes first
rows.why: Previously offered "or wait until business hours" as an option, which the rest of Part 8 rules out for equipment with a 0–60 minute target

rows.says: **Escalation step 3, for an RT call** — ventilator, cough assist, IPPB, BiPAP ST — call **the other RT** rather than the Level 1 backup, who is a DME technician
rows.why: This caveat used to appear only in 8.5, not in the chain itself

rows.says: **Power wheelchairs after hours:** advise calling back during business hours. If the patient is stuck in a vulnerable situation, advise non-emergency services or 9-1-1
rows.why: Previously said to "troubleshoot," with nothing in the manual to troubleshoot with. A basic checklist is planned

rows.says: **Concentrator troubleshooting** after hours uses the same flowchart as 7.6. Where it says to schedule a technician visit, dispatch the on-call DME technician instead
rows.why: Replaces a shorter list that had drifted — it didn't start with the distress check or mention the backup cylinder

rows.says: **The order of questions** is now also a dispatch diagram: emergency first, then existing patient, then **location**, then equipment
rows.why: Location comes before equipment because dispatch outside DFW is limited

rows.says: **A family member or caregiver** confirms their relationship to the patient, the patient's full name, and date of birth or address — then can be given order and billing details
rows.why: The rule in 1.3 changed, and after-hours callers are often family

rows.says: **While the chain is worked,** confirm the patient has a working backup — a **spare cylinder**, or a second device
rows.why: Previously listed "portable oxygen," which we don't carry

rows.says: **Menzise Richardson's** on-call number, (214) 264-0720, is now in the directory

groups.title: Stated in the manual, not taken from the after-hours guide — please verify

rows.says: **Working the chain takes time** — steps 1 to 4 take at least 90 minutes of waiting before the last backup is reached, so the 0–60 minute target assumes someone answers early

groups.title: Carried over from the after-hours guide — still accurate?

rows.says: **Hours:** 5:00 PM to 8:00 AM Monday to Friday, Central Time, and any time on weekends and company holidays
**Dispatch is DFW only.** San Antonio gets oxygen concentrator service only; Hawaii and everywhere else get none
**The on-call rota:** RTs and DME technicians alternate weeks within their own groups; check the schedule at the start of every shift
**Before the shift:** phone and laptop charged, the logbook, and the on-call schedule in the After Hours Call Log

**Dispatch by equipment:** oxygen concentrators and suction machines → the on-call DME technician, after troubleshooting · ventilators, cough assist, IPPB and BiPAP ST → the on-call RT, immediately · anything routine → business hours
**What to relay when dispatching** — including the troubleshooting already attempted
**Response targets:** Immediate, 0–60 minutes — ventilators, oxygen concentrators, suction machines · Quick, 1–2 hours — other equipment needing a prompt response
**Never contact off-schedule staff** — only the scheduled on-call personnel and designated backups
**The voicemail script**
**After the service:** create a service ticket with full detail, **and** log it in the After-Hours Logbook

# Review Packet — Part 9: Sales

**For:** Sales — **Mary Carson** (Sales Manager)
**Also for:** **April Arredondo** (Sales Eligibility) — questions marked **◆**
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-9-Sales-v3.0* (Word), or Part 9 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **9.2.1**.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from other departments' guides, not from yours. Please confirm each one reflects how your teams work.

rows.says: **Sales Eligibility can be contacted** — by email (`saleseligibility@universalmedsupply.com`) or direct transfer to its supervisor. It has no call queue ◆
rows.why: The previous guidance said the team was offshore and must not be contacted directly

rows.says: **A Qualified Lead skips PAK but still gets a PPD**, conducted by a Qualifications team member
rows.why: Previously read as though a QL skipped the PPD too

rows.says: **An evaluation more than 6 months old doesn't qualify** as a Qualified Lead — the patient needs a new appointment, and the order follows the standard path

**When a CSR can't find a patient,** they search the caller's phone number. A match on a lead means Sales is already working with the caller, so the CSR routes them to the Sales rep in the lead notes — or the relevant queue if they're unavailable: the Sales Q for power mobility, the PAP Q for PAP
rows.why: New. Previously this appeared only in 9.4, for PMD callers

rows.says: **Lead Resolutions notes** use the same format and wording as any call note
rows.why: This was left open in the previous draft

rows.says: **The Eligibility Status** is now also shown as a progression diagram, with *Eligible* marked as the handoff to Power ◆

**The Power Order Process diagram** shows Sales feeding in two ways: at *Eligible* — appointment confirmed and insurance verified — or straight to Qualifications when a mobility evaluation was done in the last 6 months
rows.why: Please check that Sales' part of the picture is right

rows.says: **Fax numbers:** Sales often uses its department fax, 210-761-7887; the main UMS fax, 972-572-1112, is always acceptable for referrals

groups.title: Carried over from your guide — still accurate?

rows.says: **Scope:** Sales handles PMD leads through the Sales Q; PAP and manual wheelchair leads sit under Sales but have their own queues — the PAP Q and the Sales MWC Q
**The Sales process** — eight stages, from lead outreach to the handoff to Power
**The appointment must be specifically a PMD Mobility Evaluation**, and it's only *verified* once confirmed with both the patient and the provider's office
**What each Eligibility Status means**, and that the appointment statuses run in order ◆
**Eligibility doesn't end at the handoff** — if a patient's insurance changes after the order reaches Power, it goes back to Sales Eligibility ◆

**A caller interested in a PMD:** if a lead exists and isn't closed, transfer to the most recent Sales rep if available, otherwise call the Sales Q; if there's no lead, call the Sales Q with the caller's phone number and full name. CSRs ask as well as search
**The one-year PPD rule:** a PPD over a year old means a new order through Sales; under a year, Power can re-open the existing order
**Member ID callbacks:** add it to the transaction and note it — after checking the notes to confirm that's all that was needed

rows.q: **The PAP Q and Sales MWC Q** each have only a routing line in Part 9. What should a CSR know about how each works — what happens to the caller, how long it takes, and what the CSR should say?
**What do you wish a CSR had already collected before transferring a call to your team?** Please answer separately for Sales Eligibility if it differs ◆

**9.4.1 — a past PMD patient who wants a new PMD** (added 2026-10-07). Five years or more since the last PMD was delivered → Sales creates a new order on the existing account. Within five years → usually a Same or Similar conflict, with a possible exception when the new PMD is an **upgrade** and the provider attests to a **significant change in physical condition or mobility needs**; for now this call also goes to **Sales**. Is all of this right? Should the within-five-years call stay with Sales or go to Power, and who decides whether the provider's attestation is enough?

p10.head:
# Review Packet — Part 10: Billing & Insurance

**For:** Billing — **Bhoj Bhatt** (Billing Manager), with **Sara (Shweta) Sharma**, **Lourdes Cano** and **Bharat Golwala** (Billing Supervisors)
**Read alongside:** *CSR-Procedures-Part-10-Billing-and-Insurance-v3.0* (Word), or Part 10 of the online manual
**Section numbers** refer to the current manual — for example, **10.13.6**.

groups.title: Changed in the September 2026 revision — please confirm
groups.intro: These came from the Customer Service Manager or from current Medicare guidance, not from the Billing guide. Several change what CSRs tell patients about money, so they matter most.

rows.says: **A verified family member or caregiver gets billing details** — including balances — and can make a payment, once they confirm their relationship to the patient, the patient's full name, and date of birth or address
rows.why: Previously family members could only give information, not receive it. This affects many billing calls

rows.says: **Hospice covers equipment related to the terminal diagnosis.** Those claims deny from the election date; **unrelated equipment can still be billed to Part B**. Billing decides which applies, and CSRs don't promise a pick-up
rows.why: Previously said all of our claims deny from the election date

rows.says: **The oxygen conserver is included in the oxygen rental** — never billed separately. It's supplied at no charge if the provider orders it; otherwise $320 out of pocket, with an ABN for Medicare patients. It's coded **A9900**
rows.why: Previously coded E1352 and described as needing a prescription "for insurance coverage." Medicare's oxygen accessory list names conserving devices as A9900, included in the rental. **If UMS has been billing E1352, please check**

rows.says: **Face-to-face and written order before delivery:** required for power wheelchairs by statute, and for some other items on CMS's list — including the **bariatric bed (E0301)**, but not the semi-electric bed. **Every hospital bed** still needs clinical notes from the last 6 months
rows.why: Previously said all hospital beds needed a face-to-face before delivery

rows.says: **A break in medical need** continues the rental if it's 60 days **plus the rest of that rental month** or less; longer starts a new 13-month rental
rows.why: Previously said "under 60 days" and "over 60 days" — imprecise near the threshold

rows.says: **Resupply timing (Medicare):** the patient confirms the refill within the **30 days** before their supply runs out; we ship no sooner than 10 days before. For a shipped order, **the ship date is the date of service**
rows.why: The contact window changed from 14 days to 30, per CMS

rows.says: **Out-of-pocket purchases** are processed by CSRs at the Item Master price, with **no sales tax** unless the order tool says so
rows.why: Previously said "plus sales tax unless there's an Rx"

rows.says: **Compliance — notes first.** CSRs answer from the compliance specialists' notes and transfer only when the notes don't settle it
**Prior authorizations are submitted by the intake team's authorization members**
rows.why: Previously said "Verification submits prior authorizations"

rows.says: **The waiver rules** are also shown as a decision diagram — QMB-only is checked first, since it waives the standard rollator fee only. **Uncommon payers** such as Workers' Compensation or the VA may pay in full, including the upgrade fee. If unsure whether UMS is enrolled in a Medicaid state, CSRs check with Eligibility

**The EAA** is processed by Billing. A CSR or Billing sends the blank form; the patient returns it with their income and expenses; usually 1–2 weeks. Out-of-pocket orders qualify for neither the EAA nor a payment plan
**Oxygen accessories are included for the full 5 years**, not only the 36-month rental — a patient shouldn't see a bill for cannulas or tubing in months 37–60 either
rows.why: Per CMS Policy Article A52514

rows.says: **No trip charge during a repair,** and a **$75 out-of-pocket charge** for a diagnostic-only visit where no repair is needed — said before the visit is booked
**Texas Medicaid as secondary** can cover items Medicare never covers, such as incontinence supplies and shower chairs

groups.title: Stated in the manual, not taken from the Billing guide — please verify

rows.says: **The 2026 figures** — the Part B deductible ($283) and Part A deductible ($1,736) were checked against CMS. **Please confirm the Medicare Advantage maximum and the Medigap high-deductible figures**
**Texas Medicaid resupply:** billed one month at a time, eligibility checked before each shipment, and the Title XIX order covers deliveries for up to six months from the provider's signature
**Timely filing:** Medicare 12 months from the date of service; Texas Medicaid 95 days
**Appeals:** a Medicare redetermination must be requested within 120 days of the MSN

groups.title: Carried over from the Billing guide — still accurate?

rows.says: **The cost estimate in five steps**, and the worked examples in 10.5.2
**QMB patients are never billed** for Medicare deductible or coinsurance
**Coordination of benefits** — only the patient can update a payer's COB record
**Capped rentals:** 13 paid months, then the patient owns the item; power wheelchairs at 15% then 6%
**Oxygen:** 36 months of rental, then no rental charge — UMS keeps ownership and keeps servicing it for up to 5 years
**Upgrade fee rules A, B and C**, and the fee amounts
**The billing scenarios** — nine worked examples
**The ABN** — Original Medicare only, signed before delivery, specific to the item and reason
**Payments:** Save Card only with explicit permission, noted on the account; Pre-Pay for out-of-pocket orders and upgrade fees
**What CSRs can and can't promise** about coverage, approval, delivery dates and fees
